newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Pepkor says sounding out black investors.
newsitem.headline: Pepkor says sounding out black investors.

text.p: One of the largest retail groups controlled by Afrikaans-speaking white management Pepkor Limited on Thursday said it was involved in ongoing talks with black investors about the possible sale of some of its assets.
"We've had several approaches from black groups, and we're talking to several of them about taking stakes in some of our operations," Pepkor chairman Christo Wiese told a news briefing.
Wiese would not name the black investors.
"There's nothing definite, we're talking... and discussing from time to time," he said.
"We've said to them we have an open door. Come with a proposition that makes sense and we will put it together," he added.

Asked to comment on the acquisition of 20 percent of Anglo American's stake in industrial group Johnnic by black-owned National Empowerment Consortium (NEC), Wiese said: "That bodes well for South Africa," he said.
Pepkor controls a wide-variety of retail stores.
Wiese said he believed the credit splurge of the last year had peaked and the cash based businesses in his group were bound to benefit from the return to cash buying by consumers.
